NEWS

May 12, 2026

We're looking for quantum physics enthusiasts to join the international EUCENTRAL Project. This is an opportunity for scientific development at a research institute and international collaboration.
We've opened recruitment for 4 positions:
2 x Research Assistant / PhD Candidate (R1)
Requirements: Master's degree in physics or related field, strong background in quantum statistical mechanics and many-body theory, programming skills
Salary: 8,000–8,900 PLN gross
2 x Postdoc / Adiunkt (R2)
Requirements: PhD in quantum physics, condensed matter physics or related field, experience in numerical computations
Salary: 10,000–10,500 PLN gross
Responsibilities:
Conducting original research on many-body open quantum systems, developing theoretical and computational tools, preparing publications, participating in international conferences. Work in the Modelling Centre for Quantum Technologies group led by Dr Federico Balducci, in collaboration with Prof. Marzena Szymańska from University College London.
What we offer:
A scientifically stimulating research environment, flexible working hours, career development support, diverse and inclusive culture where mutual support, teamwork and respect are highly valued, benefits (Multisport card subsidy, holiday subsidy, nursery and kindergarten subsidy).
Applications accepted until 30 June 2026.

Feb 16, 2026

We invite you to explore our latest research papers, now available on our website:

"Efficient Time Evolution of 2D Open-Quantum Lattice Models with Long-Range Interactions using Tensor Networks"

This paper describes how large two-dimensional arrays of long-range interacting quantum mechanical objects can be simulated using tensor network techniques, a powerful class of numerical methods. The method described is then applied to systems similar to those used in state-of-the-art atomic quantum computers.

"Antibunching in locally driven dissipative Lieb lattices"

We demonstrate how engineering specifically localised driving in dissipative Bose-Hubbard Lieb lattices can generate enhanced antibunching through a mechanism analogous to unconventional photon blockade. Our stochastic simulation results open new possibilities for engineering non-trivial quantum correlations in open lattice systems.

Find publications and details on our website. We encourage you to read the full papers!

https://eucentral.cft.edu.pl/outcomes/publications/

Jan 15, 2026

One Year of EUCENTRAL!

In January 2025, we launched EUCENTRAL – an ambitious mission to build a modelling centre for quantum technologies in Warsaw. Time to look back at what we've achieved!

What have we accomplished in 12 months?

Project kick-off
We hit the ground running – our launch conference in March brought together about 80 guests from academia, industry and media. We launched eucentral.cft.edu.pl and kicked off our communications campaign

Growing team
Jack Dunham, Dawid Hryniuk and Alex Ferrier joined our research group. We built a support team with HR and PR specialists. We're developing open-source codes, example problems and tutorials available on GitHub

Exchanges and study visits
Our team explored best practices at UCL (twice!), ICFO in Barcelona and the University of Stuttgart. Topics? Recruitment, IP management, research commercialisation, outreach, support for international teams.

Building competences
Training sessions on commercialisation, guest lectures and schooling (Abbie Bray from UCL), sharing experiences at conferences, open lecture at CNK given by Artur Ekert

This is only the beginning. Ahead of us: new challenges, recruitment drives (we're currently looking for a Team Leader!), and most importantly – building something that will reshape the European quantum technologies landscape.

Thank you for your support and stay tuned!

Dec 3, 2025

In November, our delegation (HR & Administration Specialist - Paulina Miziołek-Ambrożek and Administration Specialist - Katarzyna Rajewska) from the Center for Theoretical Physics of the Polish Academy of Sciences visited University College London, where we met with teams from the Department of Physics and Astronomy and the London Centre for Nanotechnology.
During our programme, we discussed recruitment procedures, best practices, work organisation, support for international staff, and onboarding processes. Thanks to the openness and hospitality of our hosts, we were able to learn about solutions implemented at one of Europe's leading research institutions and compare them with our own practices.
This was a valuable opportunity to exchange experiences that will help us better support our team and candidates applying to CTP PAS.
We thank our colleagues at UCL for the inspiring discussions and their willingness to share their expertise.

Dec 2, 2025

Who owns your research results? Can you commercialise your inventions?
Yesterday, Nikodem Bończa-Tomaszewski led a training session on intellectual property rights for researchers, covering the rules at CTP PAS and in Poland, illustrated with real-life examples.
The session was particularly valuable for anyone working on projects with a valorisation component, helping our team navigate the practical aspects of turning research into impact.

Nov 28, 2025

Our Director Prof. Krzysztof Pawłowski recently visited the 5th Physics Institute at the University of Stuttgart - one of Europe's leading quantum research centres.
During the study visit, he had the opportunity to see how the institute works,  and explore how Prof. Tilman Pfau combines cutting-edge science with effective management and engagement in education. The programme included meetings with research group leaders Prof. Florian Meinert, Dr Stephan Welte, Dr Ralph Klemt, Dr Harald Kuebler, and the IonMicroscope team, as well as discussions on administrative operations with Karin Otter and outreach strategies with Dr Robert Low.
These exchanges of experience help us continuously improve how we do science and share it with the world.

Nov 20, 2025

Another member joins our team. Alex Ferrier joined in November as a researcher, focusing on the development of positive P and truncated Wigner methods for spin lattices, as well as on preparing and adjusting our codes for broader use.

Nov 17, 2025

On 29-30.10.2025, a CTP PAS delegation consisting of Anna Raiter-Smiljanic, Dominika Koszade-Karwat, Remigiusz Augusiak met representatives of the Institute of Photonic Sciences (ICFO) at the ICFO headquarters in Castelldefels (Barcelona), Spain.

Our delegation met with:

- Dr. Lydia Sanmarti-Vila to discuss the best practices in outreach & dissemination, as well as potential joint activities;

- Dr. Veronica Ahufinger to learn more about ICFO's educational programme for PhDs and for visiting students;

- Cristina Morales to discuss the best practices in project management and the structure of projects team at ICFO.

- Cristina Morales and prof. Robert Sewell to discuss joint CTP PAS-ICFO project application process.
